chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Isma'il ibn Umar from Shu'ayb from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding

a man entered a village and found meat there, not knowing if it was properly slaughtered (dhabihah) or carrion (maytah). He said: 'Throw it into the fire; whatever contracts/shrinks is properly slaughtered, and whatever spreads out is carrion.'

key_terms.مَيِّتٌ: Carrion or animal that died without ritual slaughter

ai.seo_question: How to tell if meat is halal or carrion by burning it?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines a practical empirical test (istishhad) for determining the status of meat when the method of slaughter is unknown, a common issue in early Islamic communities. By observing whether the meat contracts (indicating life at slaughter) or spreads (indicating death before slaughter), the Imam provides a clear criterion for distinguishing permissible dhabihah from impermissible maytah. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on tangible evidence in resolving legal ambiguities regarding food purity.
